audit_scope.description: This batch covers: Dencun meta-EIP (EIP-7569, no external entities), eth_chainId RPC method (EIP-695), gas refund reduction (EIP-3529, no external entities), silent signing permissions (EIP-5345), and BLS remote signer API (EIP-3030). EIP-3030 involves CL validator signing infrastructure.

misclassified_entities.reason: From EIP-5345: 'Blockchain Network' receiving broadcast transactions is the system itself, not an external entity crossing a trust boundary.
From EIP-3030: 'Request Processing' pipeline that may produce errors is an internal component of the BLS remote signer, not an external entity.

trusted_external_entities.name: JSON-RPC Client (eth_chainId)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: From EIP-695: external applications query chain ID via unauthenticated JSON-RPC. While this is a read-only query, the response is critical for replay protection. Clients receiving chain ID from untrusted RPC providers must verify it independently.

trusted_external_entities.name: Wallet Application (Chain ID Consumer)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: From EIP-695: wallet applications query chain ID for EIP-155 replay-protected transaction signing. A wallet connected to a malicious RPC provider could receive an incorrect chain ID, leading to transactions valid on a different chain.

trusted_external_entities.name: dApp via Silent Signing API (EIP-5345)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: From EIP-5345: dApps request silent signing permissions to submit transactions without per-transaction user approval. This is a high-risk interface as a compromised or malicious dApp could drain funds within granted permission bounds. All permission constraints (amount limits, contract allowlists, expiry) must be enforced.

trusted_external_entities.name: Wallet User (Permission Granter)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: From EIP-5345: users grant silent signing permissions to applications. Users may be socially engineered into granting overly permissive access. The wallet must present clear permission scope and provide easy revocation.

trusted_external_entities.name: Untrusted/Malicious Application (Silent Signing Abuse)
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Silent signing API with granted permissions
trusted_external_entities.rationale: From EIP-5345: a malicious application with granted silent signing permissions could attempt to drain user funds up to the permission limit. The wallet must enforce all permission constraints (value limits, contract restrictions, time expiry) and validate permissionSecret.

trusted_external_entities.name: Validator Client via HTTP (BLS Signing Requests)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: From EIP-3030: validator clients send signing requests to the BLS remote signer over HTTP. The validator client is semi-trusted as it should be operated by the same entity as the signer, but the network channel may be untrusted. TLS should be used. The signer must still validate all requests and may implement slashing protection.

trusted_external_entities.name: HSM or Secrets Manager (Key Storage)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: From EIP-3030: the HSM or secrets manager holds BLS private keys. It is semi-trusted as a hardened component, but compromise would be catastrophic. The signer depends on it for correct key material. Access controls and audit logging are critical.

trusted_external_entities.name: Untrusted Network (BLS Signing Channel)
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Network layer between validator client and remote signer
trusted_external_entities.rationale: From EIP-3030: signing requests traverse a potentially untrusted network. Man-in-the-middle attacks could modify signing data. TLS is essential. The signer should not trust the network layer for integrity.

trusted_external_entities.name: HTTP Client (BLS Signer API Consumer)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: From EIP-3030: any HTTP client can make requests to the signer API. Without authentication, unauthorized clients could request signatures. The API must implement authentication and the signer must validate all request parameters.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: Chain ID response must reflect the current chain configuration. Incorrect chain ID could enable replay attacks on other chains. The value must remain consistent during normal operation and only change at hard forks that modify chain ID.
Wallets must verify chain ID against known values or multiple sources. Signing with wrong chain ID enables cross-chain replay attacks. Wallets should warn users if chain ID changes unexpectedly.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Silent Signing API -> Permission Check -> Transaction Construction -> Broadcast
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Every silent-signed transaction must be validated against the granted permission: value within limits, target contract in allowlist, method selector permitted, permission not expired, permissionSecret valid. Exceeding any constraint must cause rejection.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Wallet UI -> Permission Storage -> Silent Signing Engine
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Permissions must be stored securely with cryptographic binding to the granting user. Revocation must be immediate and reliable. The wallet should enforce minimum permissionSecret entropy and display clear scope summaries.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Silent Signing API -> Permission Enforcement -> Transaction Rejection/Approval
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Malicious apps will attempt to maximize extraction within permission bounds. All constraints must be enforced atomically. Running totals of value spent must be tracked accurately. Permission expiry must be checked server-side, not trusted from the client.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: HTTP POST /api/v1/sign/:identifier -> Key Lookup -> BLS Signing -> Response
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Signer must verify the public key identifier exists. Signing data should be validated for expected format. Slashing protection database should prevent signing conflicting messages. TLS should secure the channel. Authentication should verify the caller is authorized.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: HSM/Secrets API -> Key Material -> BLS Signing Operation
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Key material must never be exposed outside the signing boundary. HSM should enforce access policies. Key retrieval must be audited. Compromise of the HSM would allow arbitrary signing, so physical and logical security are paramount.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Network Layer -> TLS Termination -> HTTP API
boundary_edges.security_assumption: All communication between validator client and remote signer must use TLS to prevent MITM attacks. Certificate validation must be enforced. Network-level attackers should not be able to inject or modify signing requests.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: HTTP API -> Authentication -> Request Validation -> Response
boundary_edges.security_assumption: API must authenticate callers. Unauthenticated requests to sign or list keys must be rejected. Rate limiting should prevent brute-force attacks. Error responses must not leak sensitive information about key existence or signing state.
